Rewrite your own text more clearly

Paraphrasing means saying the same idea in a different way. Use it when a sentence feels too long or when your first draft does not explain the point clearly.

For example, “The tool can assist users in the process of improving their written communication” could become “The tool helps you write more clearly.” The shorter version is easier to follow.

Compare the suggestion with your original. Keep names, numbers and product facts correct. Reject a rewrite if it changes your meaning or sounds less natural than what you wrote.

Check grammar, then read the whole paragraph

A grammar check can help you spot mistakes you missed. Review each suggestion rather than accepting every change. The tool may not know the tone or product detail you need.

Read the paragraph again after editing. Make sure one sentence leads naturally to the next. Short sentences help, but your page still needs enough detail to answer the reader's question.

Make a useful summary from long notes

A summary keeps the main points in a shorter form. It can help you review an article or organize notes before starting a draft.

Decide what the summary is for. A quick study note may need key ideas. A work brief may also need names, dates and numbers. Compare the result with the source so an important detail is not lost.

Keep the full source for anything you may need to check later. A short summary is a guide to the material, not a replacement for reading important details.
